quorum.kill_rule: one verified counterexample kills a claim however many lanes confirmed it, and it must be a cited line reproduced with sed -n at HEAD; an absence is verified only by the judge's own search over all of src/ and tests/; a judgment question inside a claim is answered in the reason and does not decide the ruling. Round two's lane 1 raised three refutations and all three judges rejected them: apply prints d.detail, which comes from the detectors.
refuted_claims: That no report is constructed without DriftReport::new. The lockless path built its report as a struct literal, so its census never learned which resources went unmeasured and unmeasured_total was 0 on every lockless run. Corrected: the invariant holds for reports built by DriftReport::new; at the round-one head the lockless path built its own and skipped the marking.

That apply behaviour is unchanged. Apply prints each finding's detail and this change rewrote it. Corrected: apply still consumes every finding from detect_drift_full and still plans to reconcile an unmeasured resource, exactly as it did the old MISSING one; the line it prints now says `not measured` where it said `not accessible`.

That the tests discriminate. No test asserted that the image or task detectors emit UNMEASURED — both arms existed and nothing would have caught their removal. Corrected: the tests discriminated for the file path only; the image and task arms were implemented, claimed and untested until this head.

That paiml/infra's drift-tripwire.sh will now SEE unmeasured resources outside findings. It reads findings, drift_count and machines_checked and nothing else. Corrected: it will not see them, it is blind to them — drift_count 0 against 0 findings, exit 0, `no unexcused drift` for a host that answered nothing. Fixed downstream in paiml/infra#561.
lane_errors: the round-two teamwork lane ended with `LANE ISOLATION VIOLATED — a shared ref changed`. The ref was moved by the orchestrator's own commit in another worktree while the lane ran; the reflog names that commit and its author, and the lane's clone was removed byte-identical. The check credits every shared-ref change to the lane and cannot tell a lane's write from a concurrent commit by the party that dispatched it.

systems: Nagios (a plugin exits 0/1/2/3 and check_by_ssh exits UNKNOWN when it cannot reach the target; CRITICAL outranks UNKNOWN, so a caller alerting only on CRITICAL treats an unreachable host as fine)
Prometheus (reachability is its own series, up == 0; threshold queries over an unscraped target return nothing and fire nothing, so without an alert on up == 0 a dead target looks clean)
Terraform (plan -detailed-exitcode exits 1 for an error and 2 for a diff; the error halts the run, so it wins over the diff and the caller never sees a false clean)
crux.verdict: accept-with-two-disclosures(the separation MATCHES prior art — UNMEASURED is its own state, as UNKNOWN and up == 0 are, folded into neither drift nor clean — and the precedence matches Nagios, where drift wins as CRITICAL outranks UNKNOWN. Two points do NOT match and both predate this change: a tripwire run with drift exits 1 rather than the drift class 10, because the error string is `N drift finding(s)` and the legacy classifier at src/core/error.rs:278 looks for `drift detected`; and without --tripwire the command exits 0 whatever it found. The MCP verb's drifted:false when only unmeasured remain is the E05 contract, which tells an agent to read drifted together with unchecked. The survey was ruled CONFIRMED by all three judges, including its two mismatches.)
